plan.title: Heart 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is whether the drug acts differently in KO than in WT heart tissue — a genotype-by-treatment interaction in a 2x2 factorial (WT/KO x vehicle/drug, n=4 per cell, 16 samples total, salmon gene counts, 12000 genes x 17 cols including gene-symbol column). This is answered by fitting a single DESeq2-style negative-binomial GLM with design ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment on all 16 samples, testing the interaction coefficient (genotype[KO]:treatment[drug]) as the primary hypothesis test, then reporting the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT; drug vs vehicle within KO) for interpretation. QC precedes the model to check the samples group by condition and that no sample is a metadata/identity outlier. Low-count filtering is minimal (DESeq2 independent filtering does the rest). Log2 fold changes for every non-single-coefficient contrast (all three reported here) are shrunk with ashr (apeglm cannot take a contrast, only a single coefficient). BH-adjusted p-values are reported per contrast, not pooled. Preranked GSEA (fgsea-equivalent via gseapy, ranked on the Wald statistic) runs separately for each of the three contrasts against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome + WikiPathways (secondary, human, in the reference store), because a set moving up in one contrast and down in another would cancel if contrasts were pooled. All scripting is Python, per the user's constraint — PyDESeq2 for the GLM/Wald test, ashr is invoked from R via rpy2 since no pure-Python ashr equivalent exists in the pool, and gseapy.prerank for enrichment. Every step is grounded in the design-knowledge service's full_plan procedure for a 4-group 2x2 interaction design at n=4/cell on human salmon counts (snapshot sha256:90c687...c5467a), and constraints/violations were checked via execute_knowledge_check (0 violations after fixing the shrink_lfc method to ashr, since apeglm was flagged as not permitted for a contrast-based interaction design).
